findings.title: Delete-cache leaves stale cache status in the event-type tab
findings.description: The `deleteCache` mutation calls only `onSuccess` and never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation does invalidate it (lines 61-64). Refresh therefore depends on the parent's `onSuccess`. The user-settings page passes `onChanged`, which invalidates the query (apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88). `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377` renders the same wrapper with no `onChanged`, so after a cache delete there, "Last updated" keeps showing the deleted timestamp until something else refetches. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in an `onSettled`, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Disconnect flow is re-implemented instead of shared
findings.description: The dropdown rebuilds the `credentials.delete` mutation with the same toasts and invalidation as `packages/features/apps/components/DisconnectIntegration.tsx:26-40`. Its confirm dialog (lines 143-154) duplicates `DisconnectIntegrationComponent` (`packages/ui/components/disconnect-calendar-integration/DisconnectIntegration.tsx:43-49`). The copies already differ on the guard. `DisconnectIntegration` blocks in-memory delegation credentials with `isDelegationCredential({ credentialId })` (DisconnectIntegration.tsx:43). The dropdown relies on the `delegationCredentialId` prop (line 68). That is equivalent today only because in-memory credentials set `delegatedToId` (packages/lib/delegationCredential/server.ts:87). Extract the mutation or dialog and reuse it.

findings.title: Cache-status read bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.description: The handler calls `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly. Other callers go through `CalendarCache.init` (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-29), which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` flag is off. The new mock method (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30) is therefore unreachable from this handler. With the flag off, any leftover cache rows still surface as "Last updated" and "Delete cached data". Use `CalendarCache.init(null)` to match the existing pattern. `deleteCacheHandler` has the same gap.

findings.title: Date is formatted with a hard-coded locale in a localized UI
findings.description: `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale, while every other string here goes through `t()`. `useLocale()` already returns `i18n` (packages/lib/hooks/useLocale.ts:10-13, 68-72), so `i18n.language` is available. Non-English users get US-format timestamps.

findings.title: `@calcom/platform-constants` is imported by `features` without a declared dependency
findings.description: This is the only file under `packages/features` that imports `@calcom/platform-constants`, and `packages/features/package.json` doesn't declare it. The package exists in the monorepo (packages/platform/constants, name `@calcom/platform-constants`), so the import resolves only through workspace hoisting. `features` is consumed by the platform atoms, which import from it (e.g. `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:4`). Declare the dependency, or move `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` to a module `features` already depends on.

findings.title: The ownership check on delete-cache has no test
findings.description: The `findFirst({ id, userId })` check is the only thing stopping one user from clearing another user's cache, and nothing tests it. `setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts` exists as a sibling, but there are no tests for `deleteCacheHandler`, the cache enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, or `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (`calendar-cache.repository.test.ts` has none). The `updatedAt` bump in `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is also untested. The existing test at `CalendarService.test.ts:664` checks only the fetch and cache calls, and that file already uses prismock. Add a cross-user case: expect a throw and no `calendarCache.deleteMany`.

findings.title: `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is written but nothing reads it
findings.description: Every cache refresh now runs `updateManyByCredentialId(credential.id, {})`, which bumps `updatedAt` on every selected calendar for the credential. I searched the calendar UI, the platform selected-calendars atoms, the Google app-store code, the cache code, and the apps folder. The only reader is the plumbing this diff adds. The "last updated" UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29-36). The write runs on every Google push notification (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/webhook.ts:46`). Its cost is small next to the Google API call, but it has no consumer. Remove it, or name the consumer. The empty `{}` update also relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behavior, which I could not verify here. Passing `updatedAt: new Date()` would make the intent explicit. The helper's `data` type (`packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400`) is `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which is wider than the single call site needs.

findings.title: Dev script writes `.env` outside the repo when run from the root
findings.description: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves against the current directory, not the script's location. Run from the repo root (`bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` into the parent directory's `.env` and creates that file if it's missing (lines 62-65). The repo's env template is at the root (`.env.example:150`), so the intended target is the root `.env`. Resolve it from the script's location, for example `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`. Nothing in the diff documents how to invoke the script, so the expected working directory is unstated.

findings.title: Script reports failure with exit code 0
findings.description: `cleanup` ends in `exit 0`, and it is also the failure path. The rate-limit branch (line 49) and the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" branch (line 58) both call it, so a caller or CI can't tell a failed tunnel from a success. The script also never checks that `tmole` exists. If it's missing, the wait loop times out silently and the script reports the generic extraction failure. Pass the exit status into `cleanup` (`cleanup 1` on failure).

findings.title: Session user object carries unused columns on every authenticated request
findings.description: `findUnlockedUserForSession` now selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` for each selected calendar. That object feeds `getUserFromSession` (packages/trpc/server/middlewares/sessionMiddleware.ts:29), which runs on authenticated tRPC requests. Nothing in this diff reads either field from it; `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` only carries them in its type. Remove them unless a consumer is added. Keeping Google channel IDs out of the session-scoped user is also the safer default.

findings.title: Stale TODO now that `updatedAt` exists
findings.description: The comment says `updatedAt` "doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table", which this diff makes false. It also suggests ordering by it, which is now possible. Update or remove the TODO.

findings.title: Migration header contradicts its SQL, and the backfill is misleading
findings.description: The generated header says the column is added "without a default value", but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. That default also backfills every existing row with the migration timestamp, so legacy cache entries will show "Last updated" as the deploy time instead of when they were written. Rows expire after 30 days (`CACHING_TIME`, calendar-cache.repository.ts:16), which bounds the error. Note it in the migration comment.

findings.title: Icon-only menu trigger has no accessible name
findings.description: The trigger is `<Button variant="icon" StartIcon="ellipsis" />` with no `aria-label` or `tooltip`, so screen readers announce it with no name. Add an `aria-label`, backed by a translation key.

findings.title: Wrapper edits change Remove visibility and reserve empty space
findings.description: The error-state card now passes `disableConnectionModification`, so Remove disappears there when modification is disabled. It was shown before, while the success card already hid it. That may be a fix, but it isn't called out. Also, the `flex w-32` wrapper is now always rendered (lines 70-79 and 123-132). Delegated credentials with no actions reserve an empty 8rem slot where nothing rendered before. Unrelated noise: `|| null` on line 98 and a stray blank line at 162.

findings.title: Unrelated edits are bundled into this change
findings.description: `findMany` drops `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` with no connection to the feature. The `FindManyArgs` comment (line 14) suggests tighter Prisma typing was avoided on purpose, so this may be intentional, but the diff gives no reason. The `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` dev tool is loosely related at most. If it isn't part of this change, split it out.

findings.title: Shell script uses a predictable `/tmp` path and BSD-only `sed -i`
findings.description: `LOG_FILE="/tmp/tmole.log"` is a fixed path that the script `rm -f`s and then redirects into. On a shared host, another user can plant a symlink there. Use `mktemp`. Also, `sed -i ''` (line 68) is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU sed. That's acceptable for a macOS dev tool, but it should be stated.

findings.title: `deleteCache` throws a plain `Error` and defines its input inline
findings.description: The not-found and not-owned case throws a plain `Error`, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logs as a server fault. Sibling handlers use `TRPCError` (`setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts:77`). For an ownership check, `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` is the better fit because it doesn't reveal whether the id exists. Separately, the router defines its input inline (`_router.tsx:28-30`, with `z.number()`, which accepts non-integers). Sibling procedures import `*.schema.ts` schemas (`_router.tsx:5-6`).

findings.title: Delete-cache ownership check is correct
findings.description: The `findFirst` filters on both `id` and `userId: user.id`, so a user can only clear cache rows for credentials they own. The `deleteMany` (lines 28-30) runs only after this check passes. The missing test is covered above.

findings.title: Translation keys used by the new UI all exist
findings.description: All 12 keys the dropdown and wrapper use are present in the English locale. The remove-app keys are at lines 1382-1386, and the cache keys (`cache_status`, `cache_last_updated`, `delete_cached_data`, and others) are at lines 3381-3387. The JSON is excluded from the diff, so this was checked against the tree directly.
